newsitem.title: USA: Dayton November same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: Dayton November same store sales up.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said Thursday same store sales for the four weeks ended November 30 rose 1.3 percent.
Net retail sales for the period increased 8.8 percent to $2.307 billion from $2.120 billion a year ago.

"November sales at Target were above plan partially due to strong sales of (Nintendo Co Ltd video game system) Nintendo 64, while Mervyn's and the Department Store Division were below expectations," Bob Ulrich, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Dayton Hudson saiad its Target division's total sales for the month rose 16.1 percent and same store sales increased seven percent. Year-to-date, Target's total sales increased 16.1 percent and comparable-store sales gained 7.2 percent.

Mervyn's total sales for the month decreased eight percent and comparable store sales were off nine percent. Year-to-date, Mervyn's total sales decreased 1.3 percent and same store sales fell 3.1 percent.

The Department Store Division's total sales for the month decreased 1.4 percent and comparable-store sales declined 10.5 percent. Year-to-date, the Department Stores total sales decreased 0.5 percent and comparable-store sales dropped 4.3 percent.

Total company sales for the 43 weeks ended November 30 were $19.16 billion, up 10.5 percent from $17.34 billion in the same period a year ago. Comparable-store sales for the 43-week period were up 3.6 percent compared with the same period last year.
